## **Overview**

**GTAPViz** is an R package designed to streamline the processing and
visualization of GTAP-CGE results. While primarily built for **GTAP
simulations, it also supports other `.har` and `.sl4` datasets**.

With intuitive commands and automated adjustments, users can create,
customize, and export high-quality visualizations for journal
publications, economic analysis, and research reports—all with minimal
coding.

## **Key Features**

This package streamlines the creation of figures and tables from `.har`
and `.sl4` results, making academic presentations effortless. Some key
features are:

- **Effortless Multi-Plot Generation** – Automatically adjusts
  dimensions, facets, and layout with minimal input.

- **Smart Plot Adjustments** – Fine-tune visuals easily without manual
  sizing or layout tweaks.

- **Dual Export Plot Formats** – Instantly save high-resolution PNG and
  PDF outputs for slides, papers, and LaTeX.

- **Publication-Ready Pivot Tables** – Generate clean tables alongside
  figures—ideal for academic papers.

- **Streamlined Styling** – Customize colors, fonts, and legends through
  simple, flexible options.

- **Powerful Yet Simple** – Built on `ggplot2`, with intuitive
  `TRUE/FALSE` switches—no advanced coding needed.

- **Self-Contained Help** – Includes a detailed vignette and internal
  help—no need to search online.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## **Installation**

`GTAPViz` package can be installed directly from CRAN (recommended)
using:

``` r

install.packages("GTAPViz")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## **Use GTAPViz with AI (MCP)**

Let an AI app (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, …) run GTAPViz for
you. You ask in plain words, it makes the figures and tables on your
computer, and it saves the R code it used so you can rerun everything
yourself.

### 1. Install (once)

Run in R:

``` r

remotes::install_github("Bodysbobb/GTAPViz")
GTAPViz::mcp_install()                  # Claude Desktop
# GTAPViz::mcp_install("claude_code")   # or "cursor"
```

Then restart the AI app.

### 2. How to use

Try the example data that comes with the package:

> Use GTAPViz to load the example data and plot welfare by region

For your own results, give it the folder with your `.sl4` and `.har`
files:

> Load my GTAP results in D:/TradeWar/in

Then just ask, for example:

- *“What experiments and regions are there?”*
- *“Plot EV, qgdp and tot by region, with the regions on the vertical
  axis.”*
- *“Show the welfare decomposition, and rename alloc_A1 to ‘Allocative
  efficiency’.”*
- *“Which sectors in SEAsia gain the most output? Top 10 only.”*
- *“Use the purdue colors, bigger fonts, and also save as PDF.”*
- *“Make an Excel table of regional results with experiments as
  columns.”*
- *“Give me the R script.”*

The AI tells you where the figures and tables were saved.

### 3. Back in R

Everything the AI does is saved as plain GTAPViz code in
`gtapviz_session.R`, in the same output folder. Open it in RStudio and
run it to recreate every figure, no AI needed.

You can also chat from inside RStudio: open the **Terminal** tab and run
`claude` (Claude Code).

More in the [AI
guide](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/articles/GTAPViz_AI.html).

# Package index

## All functions

  : Add Mapping Information to GTAP Data
- [`auto_gtap()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/auto_gtap.md)
  : Process Static GTAP Data with Simplified Parameter Structure
- [`auto_gtap_data()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/auto_gtap_data.md)
  : Process GTAP Data Automation with Flexible Output Options
- [`auto_gtap_rd()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/auto_gtap_rd.md)
  : Process GTAP Recursive Dynamic Data with Multi-Case Support
- [`comparison_plot()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/comparison_plot.md)
  : Create Comparative Bar Charts from HAR and SL4 Data
- [`convert_units()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/convert_units.md)
  : Convert Units in GTAP Data
- [`create_decomp_style()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/create_decomp_style.md)
  : Create Decomposition Area Plot Style Configuration
- [`create_export_config()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/create_export_config.md)
  : Create an Export Configuration
- [`create_label_box_vars()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/create_label_box_vars.md)
  : Create Label Box Variables Configuration
- [`create_map_style()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/create_map_style.md)
  : Create Map Style Configuration
- [`create_plot_style()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/create_plot_style.md)
  : Create a Plot Style Configuration
- [`create_title_format()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/create_title_format.md)
  : Create a Title Format Configuration
- [`create_trend_style()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/create_trend_style.md)
  : Create Trend Plot Style Configuration
- [`create_vline()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/create_vline.md)
  : Create Vertical Line Configuration
- [`decomp_area_plot()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/decomp_area_plot.md)
  : Create Decomposition Area Charts Over Time
- [`detail_plot()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/detail_plot.md)
  : Create Comprehensive Bar Charts from HAR and SL4 Data
- [`dynamic_input_name()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/dynamic_input_name.md)
  : Generate Dynamic Input Mapping for GTAP Experiments
- [`get_all_config()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/get_all_config.md)
  : Print Plot and Export Configuration Snippets
- [`get_color_palette()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/get_color_palette.md)
  : Print and Visualize Themed Color Palettes
- [`get_trend_style_config()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/get_trend_style_config.md)
  : Get Trend Plot Style Configuration Helper
- [`map_heatmap()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/map_heatmap.md)
  : Create Country/Region Heatmaps
- [`mcp_config()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/mcp_config.md)
  : Show the GTAPViz MCP Server Settings
- [`mcp_install()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/mcp_install.md)
  : Connect GTAPViz to Your AI App (One-Time Setup)
- [`mcp_serve()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/mcp_serve.md)
  : Start the GTAPViz MCP Server for AI Assistants
- [`pivot_table_with_filter()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/pivot_table_with_filter.md)
  : Export Data as an Excel Pivot Table
- [`rename_value()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/rename_value.md)
  : Rename Values in a Column
- [`report_table()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/report_table.md)
  : Generate a Structured Report Table
- [`sort_plot_data()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/sort_plot_data.md)
  : Sort GTAP Plot Data
- [`stack_plot()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/stack_plot.md)
  : Create Stacked Bar Charts for Decomposition Analysis
- [`trend_plot()`](https://www.pattawee-pp.com/GTAPViz/reference/trend_plot.md)
  : Create Time Trend Line Plots from GTAP Data
